title: RMS Teutonic, 1889 — broadside
used_for: Sheer and freeboard; two buff funnels with black caps; three pole masts; the low midship house with an open promenade round it; Trotman davits with boats stowed above the promenade.

title: RMS Germanic in the Mersey
used_for: Hull form and waterline; bow rake and counter stern; the black hull / white upper works division at the main deck.

title: SS Majestic, 1890
used_for: Deckhouse proportions and window rhythm; ventilator cowls; the sheer strake as a white band.

title: SS Paris in dry dock, 1895-96
used_for: Underwater body: keel, stem, sternpost, propeller aperture, rudder and the bilge keels.  Used for the hull section and the bow/stern detail.

title: City of Paris at sea (Jacobsen)
used_for: Sea keeping and the smoke plume at speed — the basis for the smoke and wake behaviour in the Roblox client script.

title: City of Paris, 1888
used_for: Alternative funnel/mast arrangement considered and rejected: twin screws and three masts read as a later ship.

title: Grand staircase — Teutonic (Ocean Magazine, Sept 1889)
used_for: Stair width, half landings, balustrade pattern and the glazed dome.  Our stair well is 4.7 m wide with a single flight per storey.

title: Smoking saloon — Teutonic (Ocean Magazine, Sept 1889)
used_for: Panelled to the cornice, leather settees round the walls, small tables and revolving chairs; the fireplace as the focus of the room.

title: First-class stateroom — Teutonic
used_for: Berth proportions, wardrobe, washstand, and the window arrangement; our staterooms are 2.4 m wide x 3.1 m long with one berth abreast.

title: Main saloon — Teutonic (Ocean Magazine, Sept 1889)
used_for: Long communal tables down the length; columns at the sides; the ground-glass panel that lights the saloon from the library table.

title: Library — Teutonic
used_for: Bookcases and the central ground-glass table; used for our library 6..27 m with a 4.9 x 2.9 m illuminating table.

title: Second-class staircase — Teutonic
used_for: Cheaper joinery and a narrower stair for the second class, informing the second-class circulation we modelled.
